findings.finding: Worldpanel has Tesco losing UK grocery share for four consecutive reports into the half-year end: 27.8% against 28.1% a year earlier, with Tesco sales +1.8% (12 weeks to 9 Aug) and +1.7% (to 6 Sep) against a market growing about 2.5%. NIQ total-till growth then slowed to +1.8% with units -0.1% in the 4 weeks to 5 Sep. This points to a Q2 UK LFL no better than Q1's +1.8%, while retail previews (HL, IG) still frame the half as continued share gains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026/27 (UK LFL +1.8%, soft against a strong base) moved -0.94%; Q3/Christmas 2025/26 moved -6.74%; the share-gain-led interims of Oct 2025 moved +5.28%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Worldpanel is read by every analyst, and the stock fell from 501.8p (29 Jul) to 446.1p (18 Aug) as the share loss and Shore Capital's downgrade landed. It has since recovered to 473p, and the domestic retail previews (HL 5 Oct: 'recent market share gains to have continued over the first half'; IG 28 Sep headline on 'strong market share gains') carry a narrative the panel data contradicts. If the share loss were fully priced the stock would not have recovered most of the August drop going into the print.
findings.independence: NIQ total till +1.8%, units -0.1%, 4 weeks to 5 Sep 2026 (https://retailtimes.co.uk/niq-summer-slowdown-sparks-a-september-reset-in-uk-grocery-shopping/); Worldpanel 18 Aug report, Tesco +1.8% and share down a third report in a row (https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/08/18/uk-grocery-inflation-eases-further-says-worldpanel); Worldpanel 22 Jul, Tesco 27.9% and +1.7% against a market +3.3% (https://foodmanagement.today/inflation-eases-to-2-6-as-sport-drives-grocery-purchases/)

findings.finding: The bar sits in the top half of the guide: company-compiled consensus of GBP3.25bn (Visible Alpha, 29 Apr) against a GBP3.0-3.3bn range Bernstein called conservative. Since then food inflation has fallen to 2.1-2.3%, which removes the inflation tailwind Bernstein's upper-end case relied on, and Shore Capital (12 Aug, cut to Hold, target 525p to 480p) flagged shallow summer volume and that 'cost recovery is not easy'. HL expects no change to the guide. An unchanged range, or a narrowing centred near GBP3.15-3.2bn, would sit at or below the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interims Oct 2025, guide raised to GBP2.9-3.1bn: +5.28%. Prelims Apr 2026, first FY26/27 guide (midpoint below consensus but read as conservative): +4.70%. Q3 Jan 2026, profit guide only reiterated at the top end: -6.74%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly. The consensus number is public, but the April consensus was set when the scenario was higher food inflation (Bernstein: Tesco 'should reach at least the upper end of this range' given higher food inflation and fuel prices). Worldpanel inflation has since fallen to 2.1% (Aug) and 2.3% (Sep). If the market had reset the bar, the stock would not be trading near its July level (473p against 489p at end-July) on a sector that has derated: Sainsbury's is down from 355p to 327p over the same period.
findings.independence: Shore Capital downgrade, 12 Aug 2026 (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/share-tips/stockbroker-tips/shore-capital-downgrades-tesco-to-hold,-says-its-time-to-pause-for-breath); Worldpanel inflation series (https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/08/18/uk-grocery-inflation-eases-further-says-worldpanel); Bernstein and consensus at prelims (https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/tesco-fy-2025-26-results-what-the-analysts-said-309791)

findings.finding: The buyback has been idle for two months: GBP550.0m of the GBP750m programme was bought by 31 July and no Transaction in Own Shares RNS has followed since 3 August. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean observation: buyback tranches have been announced alongside results, not on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the GBP750m size and the April 2027 completion are public. Only an upsized programme would be new, and I have no evidence of one.
